reasoning_content:
The second server failed to start due to a port conflict with the first instance, which is expected since port 5195 was already in use. I'm checking the logs to confirm this is the source of the error and then I'll shut down my instance to clean up.

The real question is whether the running server actually has the correct AuthCookie from appsettings.json. When the binder loaded defaults during the first request, it read AuthCookie as "UIH234...", which matched what I was testing. But now subsequent requests are failing even though the config should be static. I'm wondering if there's a race condition during assembly load — maybe the Binder was scanning the Bovis.Web.dll assembly before the appsettings values were fully bound, or if a newly loaded assembly triggered a reprocessing that overwrote the config.

Actually, looking at the LoadDefaults logic, it only processes an assembly once and skips if the config value is null, so it can't unbind a value. But I'm realizing I might be misinterpreting the grep results — when I searched for "Bovis Bohrs" in the response, it should only match the full "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung" text in the navbar, and that count of 0 in test A really does mean no admin content was rendered.

The key difference I'm noticing is that the first test used the full string "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung" while the later controlled test used just "nav-item" — and the no-admin layout has no nav-item, so that's consistent. But looking at the sequence: the first request at 12:46:58 definitely rendered the admin layout with the full navbar and branding, but everything from 12:48:31 onward, even the root path with the cookie, shows no admin content. The requests are identical and the cookie value comes from the same source, so why did it work once and then never again? I'm wondering if the AuthCookie static field got reinitialized somehow between those two time points.

I'm checking whether something in the code could be resetting the cookie to a random value. The only random source is in the Globals class initializer, and the ConfigurableBinder only sets values if they're not null. The assembly processing is guarded by a processed set, so it shouldn't reinitialize. But I'm realizing the Globals class has both a default initializer and a [Configurable] attribute, so I need to think through the exact sequence of when the class loads and when the binder runs.

Looking at the test timeline more carefully, the first curl request at 12:46:58 showed the admin layout, but subsequent requests didn't. I'm wondering if the first test was actually testing a different scenario—maybe the cookie wasn't being sent correctly, or there's something else going on with how the auth state is being validated between requests. So the real test is to create a fresh cookie that I control, set it in a temporary appsettings override, and verify that auth works from the start. If a fresh instance with a known cookie renders admin consistently, then the auth system is sound and the original server's one-off behavior is just noise from an unknown prior state. But if even a fresh instance fails, then there's a genuine auth bug. I'll run a quick test on port 5197 with a custom cookie value in a temp directory, then clean up after. The binder should bind AuthCookie at startup when I create the WebApplication, and the /app path will show admin status if it's working. I'll make sure the cookie value is distinct from the original to avoid any confusion.

Before running the test, I should clean up the old process from the earlier failed attempt to avoid any leftover state.The test server on 5197 crashed, likely due to a port conflict with the existing instance on 5195. I'll clean up that instance and run the definitive probe instead.
